title: ATM / Banking Queue Management
short_description: Learn how banks and ATM systems manage customer queues, reuse fixed service slots, process requests using stacks, schedule customer services, and reduce waiting time efficiently.

real_world_context.problem: A bank branch or ATM network needs to manage customers waiting for services and process requests in an organized manner. The system must maintain customer order, efficiently reuse limited request slots, handle service requests in reverse order when required, schedule non-overlapping appointments, and reduce overall customer waiting time.
real_world_context.why_it_matters: Efficient queue management and scheduling algorithms help banking systems organize customer requests, utilize limited service resources, schedule appointments effectively, and reduce waiting times as the number of customers increases.

learning_objectives: Understand how queues maintain the order of customers waiting for banking services.
Apply FIFO queue operations to process customers in their arrival order.
Understand how circular queues efficiently reuse fixed-size service slots.
Apply stack operations to process service requests in reverse order.
Use Activity Selection to schedule the maximum number of non-overlapping customer services.
Apply Greedy techniques to minimize the total waiting time of customers.
Understand how sorting can support efficient scheduling and service-order decisions.
Understand why appropriate data structures and algorithms are important for managing banking queues efficiently.

real_world_mapping.customer: Person waiting for a banking service
real_world_mapping.service_request: Request submitted by a customer for a banking service
real_world_mapping.waiting_queue: Queue containing customers waiting to be served
real_world_mapping.service_slot: Fixed position available for temporarily storing ATM or banking requests
real_world_mapping.circular_queue: Fixed-size queue that reuses positions released after dequeue operations
real_world_mapping.service_request_sequence: Sequence of banking requests that can be processed using stack operations
real_world_mapping.appointment: Scheduled customer service with a start and end time
real_world_mapping.service_counter: Banking counter where customers receive services
real_world_mapping.service_time: Amount of time required to serve a customer
real_world_mapping.waiting_time: Time a customer waits before their service begins
real_world_mapping.customer_scheduling: Process of arranging customers or appointments for efficient service

completion_message: You have completed the ATM / Banking Queue Management mission. You have learned how queues, circular queues, stacks, activity selection, and greedy scheduling can be applied to customer management, service scheduling, resource reuse, and waiting-time optimization in banking systems.
